title: River bluff-to-value ratios
description: Five questions on the indifference principle and the optimal bluff fraction.

questions.prompt: Pot 50bb, river bet 50bb. What is the GTO bluff fraction (in %, 1 decimal)?
questions.explanation: b = B / (P + 2B) = 50 / (50 + 100) = 33.3%. For a pot-sized river bet, ~1/3 of the betting range should be bluffs, ~2/3 value.

questions.prompt: For a 1/2-pot river bet, the bluff:value ratio is 1:3. What share of the bets should be bluffs (in %, integer)?
questions.explanation: Bluffs / (Bluffs + Value) = 1 / 4 = 25%. The smaller the bet, the smaller the bluff share — small bets give villain great odds, so you can threaten less often.

questions.prompt: What does the indifference condition aim to make true?

choices.text: The bluffer's EV when called equals the EV when folded.
The defender is indifferent between calling and folding because both have EV = 0 against the betting range.
The defender's call wins exactly the bet size.
Both players have the same hand strength on average.

questions.explanation: Indifference: defender's call has EV = 0 against the betting range, so they cannot exploit you by deviating. This is the GTO equilibrium for the river.

questions.prompt: Against a microstakes calling station, you should still bluff at the GTO ratio — anything else is exploitable.
questions.explanation: GTO ratios are an unexploitable baseline; against under-folding opponents you should bluff *less* than GTO — often near zero. Their call rate already exceeds α, so any bluff is -EV.

questions.prompt: Why do the river bluff:value ratios not apply directly to flop or turn betting? Select all that apply.

choices.text: On earlier streets, 'bluffs' are usually semi-bluffs with showdown equity.
The pot will continue to be wagered on later streets, complicating the EV calculation.
There is no β formula for earlier streets — only α.
Solver outputs show different value/bluff ratios at flop, turn, and river.

questions.explanation: Semi-bluffs and future betting both shift the math. Solvers show ~1/3 value on the flop, ~1/2 on the turn, ~2/3 on the river. The α formula does still apply — it's just not the whole story.
